clue.text: Everyone joins in lousy song

indicators.note: one word joining in another goes into the middle of it, so the word for everyone sits inside

parts.note: lousy means bad
everyone means all

explanation.surface: The whole crowd joins in singing a dreadful song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousy' looks like a comment on the singing, but it only supplies the outer word, which 'joins in' splits around the word for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative song or slow sentimental number.

clue.text: Signal to get football player (no amateur!) on

indicators.note: no in brackets tells us to leave out the amateur from the footballer's name

parts.note: David Beckham, the England footballer
a ham is an amateur, especially an amateur radio operator
taken as written

explanation.surface: A coach gestures to bring on a professional footballer as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes HAM from BECKHAM, leaving BECK. HAM is a slang word for an amateur performer or radio enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: To beckon is to summon someone with a gesture, a kind of signal.

clue.text: He, valiant, destroyed monster

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the letters of the two words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A brave hero slays a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges the letters of HE and VALIANT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leviathan is a huge sea beast of the Bible, so any giant creature.

clue.text: Biological substance extractable from gentian

indicators.note: something extractable can be drawn out of a plant and remade, so the plant name's letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Some biochemical can be drawn from the gentian plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extractable from' signals rearranging the letters of GENTIAN; gentian is an alpine plant used in herbal medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: An antigen is a molecule that provokes the immune system to make antibodies.

clue.text: Devon town not quite right, one wanting money

indicators.note: not quite means the town's name stops short of its final letter

parts.note: Crediton is a market town in Devon, a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: A Devon town is not quite correct, and someone there wants their money back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the last letter N of CREDITON, leaving CREDITO, then R is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person or body owed a debt by someone else.

clue.text: Where in America you may find a ruddy chicken?

definitions.text: Where in America you may find a ruddy chicken?

parts.words: Where in America you may find a ruddy chicken?
parts.note: the reddish chicken is a well-known breed named after a small US state in New England, so the state is where it hails from

explanation.surface: Asking which part of America is home to a red-faced hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhode Island Red is a famous breed of red-feathered domestic fowl named after that state.

clue.text: Regret starts with doubt expressed privately over stories

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed over another comes before it
starts with tells us to take the opening letters of the next three words

parts.note: lore is a body of traditional stories

explanation.surface: Someone privately voices misgivings about the tales being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts with' gives D, E and P from doubt, expressed, privately; 'over' puts that above LORE in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplore something is to lament or strongly disapprove of it.

clue.text: What a stew - - that hidden flavour!

indicators.note: hidden says the letters sit concealed inside the run of words what a stew

explanation.surface: A cook exclaims at a stew whose flavour has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' points to the letters inside whaTASTEw.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is the savour of food, the same as its flavour.

clue.text: Artist and I interrupting ceremonies, being freaks

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

indicators.note: interrupting means the letter breaks into the middle of the word for ceremonies

parts.note: rites are ceremonies
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter and I break up some solemn rituals, an odd sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' gives the Royal Academician abbreviation, a crossword staple; only the letter I does the 'interrupting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarities are rare things or oddities, unusual specimens much like freaks of nature.

clue.text: The thing nipped by rodent, creating a hole

indicators.note: nipped by means held between the rodent's letters as if in its teeth

parts.note: a cavy is a guinea pig or related South American rodent
the thing means it

explanation.surface: A guinea pig gnaws something and makes a hole in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A cavy is the family name for the guinea pig; 'nipped by' pictures the rodent's teeth closing on the thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavity is a hollow space or hole, as in a tooth.

clue.text: Creative type going from bar to bar?

definitions.text: Creative type going from bar to bar?

parts.words: Creative type going from bar to bar?
parts.note: suggests a pub crawler, but the bars are measures of written music filled one after another

explanation.surface: An artistic person on a pub crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of music works through a score measure by measure, each measure being a bar.

clue.text: Silly don, eager to imbibe a drink

indicators.note: to imbibe is to take in, so the jumble holds the letter inside
silly suggests the letters of don and eager are jumbled up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A foolish academic, keen to have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' jumbles the two words into ORANGEDE, and 'to imbibe' then drinks in the single A.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a sweet fizzy soft drink flavoured with citrus fruit.

clue.text: Mark not seen in an English cafe?

definitions.text: Mark not seen in an English cafe?

parts.words: Mark not seen in an English cafe?
parts.note: the French spelling of the word for a coffee shop carries a small mark over its final e, which English usually leaves off

explanation.surface: Looking for a stain or score that never appears in a British coffee shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word café has a rising diacritic over the e, usually dropped in English writing.

clue.text: Deliveries should come ahead of time — that's obvious

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: A remark that the post ought to arrive early, which goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler sends down six deliveries in an over; here OVER comes ahead of T.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden.

clue.text: Gee — horrendous working for university award!

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation at some ghastly effort toward a qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges GEE and HORRENDOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bachelor's qualification at a higher level than an ordinary pass.

clue.text: Soldiers coming to a side road on the way back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a turning is a road branching off another

explanation.surface: Troops come to a side road while heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Returning means going or coming back, so travelling home.

clue.text: I get a tad bothered and worked up

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed, so the letters of those words are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone admits to getting a little flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' rearranges the letters of I GET A TAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means anxious and excited, just as worked up does.

clue.text: Information on anaesthetic is collected by appropriate medical practitioner

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
ether was an early general anaesthetic

indicators.note: collected by means taken up and held inside the word for appropriate

parts.note: apt means appropriate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor is gathering facts about an anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' makes APIST, the word for appropriate gathering in the little word 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: This specialist treats disorders by altering a patient's DNA, a kind of physician or clinician.

clue.text: Vehicle that is used for cinema advertising

definitions.text: that is used for cinema advertising

explanation.surface: A van that advertises films at the cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailer is a wheeled unit towed behind a car, and also a short preview of a coming film.

clue.text: Set up like a church choir member?

explanation.surface: Is it established like a singer seated in the chancel?
explanation.definitionFit: To install is to put in place; split in two it says a chorister sits in a choir stall.

clue.text: E.g. Bowler getting on a bit and no longer favoured

parts.note: getting on a bit is an idiom for growing old
a bowler is a kind of hard round hat

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler ageing and losing selection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' wants to be the cricketer, but here it is the round felt hat worn by City gents.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something stale and out of fashion.

clue.text: Us city volunteers nobbling a politician

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: Reservists take hold of a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, the British army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a city on the Gulf coast of Florida.

clue.text: St Thomas's custom and practice

explanation.surface: The habits and observances of a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Thomas More was a saint, so the possessive is his; mores are a society's accepted conventions.

clue.text: Public register's showing bounder among the stars

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a bounder
astral means of or among the stars

explanation.surface: A list of names reveals a rogue among the celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadastral describes a cadastre, an official register of land ownership and values.

clue.text: The daughter jumps over stream, getting excited

indicators.note: jumping over a stream means straddling it, so the stream sits within the other letters

parts.note: a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A girl leaps across a brook, full of glee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumps over' pictures the daughter straddling the brook, so the stream's letters sit inside THED.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrilled means delighted and stirred up with pleasure.

clue.text: Ill-mannered adult tucking into egg and cod?

indicators.note: tucking into means getting inside, so the letter is placed within the meal

parts.note: an egg is shaped like O
a cod is a fish
A is the film certificate for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up digs into a plate of egg and cod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' sets A between O and FISH; the question mark flags cod as only an example of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Oafish means loutish and clumsy, the manners of a boor.

clue.text: Individual's hell, a holiday island

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, so hell
Crete is a Greek island popular with holidaymakers

explanation.surface: One person's nightmare is a Mediterranean resort.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Individual stands for is, linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, each unit standing alone.

clue.text: Disease across nearly all the home-country

indicators.note: nearly all means everything except the final letter of the word

parts.note: Blighty is old British slang, from soldiers abroad, for Britain or England

explanation.surface: An illness spreads over most of the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly all' drops the last letter of BLIGHTY, British soldiers' slang for home.
explanation.definitionFit: Blight is a plant disease that withers crops.
